miniProject.title: Versioned corpus with replayable token exposure
miniProject.brief: Create `lmlab`, the Python and PyTorch repository for your versioned language-model study. Build a bounded corpus pipeline whose filtering decisions, tokenizer costs and training batches can be independently audited on your machine, using pinned libraries from the units and no paid API.
steps: Create `lmlab`: `data/` (corpus/tokenizer/shards), `model/` (decoders), `train/` (training/recovery), `scaling/` (fits), `eval/` (tasks/graders), `adapt/` (SFT/distillation), `pref/` (preferences), `rl/` (rollouts/updates), `mm/` (image-text), `safety/` (attacks/release), `registry/` (run manifests), `tests/` and `reports/` (evidence). Choose a bounded behavior question; retain a source-rights ledger checked against acquisition records.

Build a record-preserving WARC iterator and extraction, language and quality stages in `data/`. Pass CS336 Assignment 4 extraction, language-ID and quality tests; reuse your language-retention table and hand-label extraction losses and per-rule false positives by slice, retaining intervals and normalization decisions.

Deduplicate with collision-safe exact matching and MinHash candidates verified by exact Jaccard. Audit evaluation containment, PII masking and word-list versus classifier harm decisions against planted controls and hand labels; retain clusters, reviewed spans, masked evidence, slice intervals and detector blind spots.

Version the project tokenizer and reuse your FLORES-200 premium table against another tokenizer, checking sentence alignment and totals independently. Add your repository's code slice and indentation perturbation; retain revisions, language-ID retention, fertility and context-budget consequences without comparing cross-tokenizer token losses.

Build packing masks and a token-weighted, epoch-capped mixture sampler. Check packed logits against separate-document execution, document swaps and position offsets; compare realized shares with analytical expectations. Retain boundary, truncation and tail rules, valid-target counts, unique and processed exposure, and assumption-labeled effective-token estimates.

Publish checksummed shards and content-addressed manifests with a bidirectional batch-lineage index. Regenerate arbitrary batches in fresh processes and compare resumed order against uninterrupted iteration; inject corruption and data/tokenizer mismatches. Retain dropped tails, refusal tests and checkpoint links to data, tokenizer and sampler identity.

Gate the foundation decoder on frozen-batch loss, gradient, mask and analytical parameter/FLOP-count oracles before matched-token, equally tuned filtered-versus-unfiltered comparisons across paired seeds. Keep held-out outcomes and failed attempts; regenerate artifacts and a Data Cards Playbook card from raw inputs and stage logs.
deliverables: The `data/` pipeline, tokenizer, checksummed shards and batch-lineage index with independent regression tests.
Source-rights ledger, filter and contamination audits, tokenizer tables and a version-bound data card.
Matched filtering comparison with held-out records, all-attempt manifests and a clean regeneration transcript.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 4 extraction tests
checks.note: Pass the extraction fixture; add record-boundary and hand-reviewed main-content checks.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 4 language identification tests
checks.note: Pass label checks; retain your own per-language threshold and normalization audit.

checks.name: CS336 Assignment 4 quality tests
checks.note: Pass rule and classifier fixtures; they do not establish quality or false-positive rates.

checks.name: FLORES-200 parallel-sentence audit
checks.note: Use aligned sentences as the comparison reference; preserve split, tokenizer revisions and counting checks.

rubric.pass: Hand labels and planted controls check pipeline decisions; rights unknowns and masked evidence remain visible. Filtering comparisons follow frozen-batch oracles, matched budgets and paired seeds, preserving held-out outcomes and failed attempts.
rubric.strong: A matched unique-data control separates filtering from scarcity; a reviewed near-miss changes a decision and becomes a privacy-preserving regression.

rubric.pass: Your separate-document and perturbation oracles check attention and loss boundaries; analytical shares check the capped sampler. Tokenizer audits distinguish processed, unique and assumed effective tokens.
rubric.strong: A document-weighted sampler and a leaking mask each fail targeted regressions before their repairs pass.

rubric.pass: Fresh-process replay and interrupted-order tests match batch identities; content tampering and identity mismatches fail. Raw-input regeneration reproduces manifests, and checkpoints resolve to source spans.
rubric.strong: A deletion request identifies affected batches and checkpoints, while a metadata-only rewrite preserves content identity.

miniProject.feedsInto: Corpus, tokenizer, packing contracts and batch lineage feed Architecture and Numerics, Pretraining Reliability, scaling and contamination evaluation; immutable identities and regeneration evidence become the capstone baseline package.
